title: IHttpClientFactory resilience retries and timeouts
concepts: An outbound HTTP call crosses process and network boundaries. Model it as a dependency operation with explicit destination, deadline, cancellation, response handling, and failure policy. HttpClient owns connection pooling through its handler; repeatedly constructing and disposing clients can create socket pressure, while a forever-lived client can retain stale DNS results unless its connection lifetime is managed.

IHttpClientFactory separates short-lived HttpClient objects from cached underlying handlers, centralizes configuration, and composes outgoing DelegatingHandler middleware. Named clients provide configuration by logical name; typed clients wrap a configured client behind an application-specific API. Handler scopes are separate from incoming ASP.NET request scopes, so scoped request state must not be captured in pooled handlers.

Resilience strategies must fit the operation's semantics. Retry only transient failures when repeating the operation is safe, bound attempts and total time, respect server backoff where applicable, and avoid multiplying retries across layers. A timeout cancels work but cannot guarantee a remote server did not complete it. Hedging sends concurrent alternative attempts and can amplify load; circuit breakers and concurrency limits protect dependencies during sustained failure.

The current Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience package builds resilience pipelines with Polly-based strategies. Standard resilience handlers are configured on IHttpClientBuilder; they do not make every operation safe to repeat. Prefer idempotency or a server-supported idempotency key for retried writes, and observe cancellation, status codes, retry delays, and downstream load.

Use Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience with AddStandardResilienceHandler and AddStandardHedgingHandler for the current integrated setup. The resilience and Http extensions packages are separately versioned from the .NET runtime; pin and validate compatible package versions rather than assuming package version equals target framework version.

The legacy Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly integration remains a distinct package and API surface. Teach AddPolicyHandler only as migration context when the target application still uses that package; don't mix old policy registration names into the current standard resilience API inventory.

IHttpClientFactory, typed and named clients, handler pooling, System.Net.Http.Json helpers, and SocketsHttpHandler lifetime controls remain current. The key DNS behavior is controlled by connection reuse and PooledConnectionLifetime, not by constructing a new HttpClient per request.

scopeExclusions: General HTTP protocol semantics, authentication protocols, CORS, and inbound ASP.NET Core HTTP middleware are covered in the web fundamentals and security tracks.

Domain-specific retry safety, idempotency storage, fallback content, and service-level objectives depend on the calling operation and are taught as design decisions rather than universal framework behavior.
Full Polly API catalog and resilience pipeline customization beyond HTTP are covered in architecture and resilience topics; this manifest names only the HTTP integration surfaces needed here.
Third-party generated API clients are covered as integration patterns; each generator maintains its own independent client and configuration APIs.
